craft_notes: Sthāyin: heroes' rule — warrior-grade distinction. Sanskrit-first: vīroddeśena tu (by-heroes-rule-but) kept; five substances listed whole (raṇareṇu→śmaśānanabhaḥ); candrārkau du. kept sun-and-moon; nirvikalpakaḥ closes. Rows: 9 (five-substance catalogue), 1 (‘undiscriminating’ closes — nirvikalpa end-weight), 7 declined — the rule speaks, no one is addressed. Close: 'the self undiscriminating.' Rejected: ‘heroes’ ceremony’ — killed: vīroddeśa is rule-of-heroes, not ritual-name; placing moon before sun — killed: candrārkau order kept. Read aloud: NOW-HER-oes' RULE — THE-dis-TINC-tion: BAT-tle-DUST, HER-o-WA-ter, GREAT-wind, HER-o-ASH, THE-cre-Ma-tion-GROUND-sky — SUN and-MOON PLACED-in-THEM, THE-self un-DIS-CRIM-i-NA-ting.

lines: the cremation-ground sky — sun and moon placed in them,
l4.sanskrit_cite: vīroddeśena tu viśeṣaḥ tad yathā raṇareṇuḥ vīrāmbhaḥ mahāmarut vīrabhasma śmaśānanabhaḥ tadupahitau candrārkau ātmā nirvikalpakaḥ

reads_against.argmap: What is the heroes' distinction in bathing? → Vīroddeśa's five hero-substances with candrārkau placed are the warrior-grade bath; the ātman there is nirvikalpaka — undiscriminating.
c1_essence: Heroes-rule sets the five substances — battle-dust to cremation-ground sky — with sun-moon placed and the self undiscriminating.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
